migration.migration_reason: A preserved paid Semantic Compression metric shard with the same scientific experiment identity as the recertified owner was rebound to the current canonical catalog. Explicit legacy fragments, when present, matched exactly; the current metric validator re-checks the result.

limitations: This is a single-worker, bounded-effort annotation pass over all 44 frozen probes for one language; it was not independently cross-checked by a second annotator as pre_measurement_validation V1-V4 would ultimately require for full publication.

The normalization formula (100*2^(-mean_log2B)) is this worker's documented, monotonic choice for turning the 'lower is better' raw branching metric into the required 0-100 'higher is better' scale; it is recorded here so the runner/aggregator can verify or replace it consistently across all language shards if a different frozen normalization is adopted centrally.
F05.P1's B_i=6 is taken directly from the frozen spec 6.1.4.B enumerated baseline rather than independently re-derived, per the probe's own SCORING NOTE.
metric.semantic_determinacy.methodology_basis: spec 6.1.3.B (semantic_compression.md): raw value is mean(log2(B_i)) over the fixed probes, where B_i is the number of materially different semantic interpretations compatible with the probe's local surface form before consulting external declarations/whole-program facts. Lower mean(log2(B_i)) is better. This shard reports Zig only.

normalization_rule.rationale: mean_log2B=0 (every probe fully determinate, B_i=1 for all) maps to 100 (best). Each doubling of the average branching factor halves the score (mean_log2B=1 -> 50; mean_log2B=2.585 i.e. average B=6 -> ~16.7). This is a monotonic, documented, symmetric inversion of the raw 'lower is better' branching count into the required 0-100 'higher is better' scale; the same formula would be applied identically to any language.

per_probe_branching.note: const n = 7; return n; — value/storage/mutability/init/type all fixed by const-binding + function return type, no ambiguity.
var counter: i64 = 0; const LIMIT: i64 = 100; — var/const distinction is a language-enforced binary with a single reading.
var v: i32 = undefined; then both-arm branch assignment — Zig's definite-assignment analysis plus explicit `undefined` leaves one reading.
var buf: [16]u8 = undefined; — explicit undefined marker, single reading (genuinely uninitialized, not zero-filled).

x += 1; on a fixed-width signed int — Zig's plain arithmetic operators panic on overflow in Debug/ReleaseSafe but are undefined behavior in ReleaseFast/ReleaseSmall; the local operator glyph alone is compatible with either behavior without knowing the compiler mode (a global configuration fact), so B_i=2. (The frozen recipe pins ReleaseSafe, which is a locality/support fact, not a change to this local-form branching count.)
xs.items[1] = 42; on an ArrayList's backing slice — element assignment through an already-bound name is a single in-place write with a checked-bounds panic; no alternate reading.
var port = &slot; port.* = 9; — explicit address-of and explicit dereference; single reading.
const window: []const i32 = xs.items[0..]; — slices are always non-copying views in Zig by language rule, single reading.
Pointer/reference identity via `==` on pointer values routed through a one-element container — Zig pointer equality is unambiguously address comparison, single reading.

Bare call f(x) where x is Zig's normal growable-sequence type (ArrayList) — per spec 6.1.4.B's own enumerated baseline, the call-site form alone (without f's signature) is compatible with: callee cannot observe caller's object; may read only; may write elements; may replace/resize; may retain the alias; or received a copy — Zig's plain call syntax does not disambiguate any of these locally (structs/slices pass by value, but ArrayList's internal pointer means writes to elements can still be caller-visible), so the full 6-way baseline applies as it does for every language without a call-site-visible aliasing marker.
fn put(cell: *i32) void { cell.* = 12; } called as put(&cell); — explicit pointer parameter type and explicit address-of at the call site jointly leave one reading: callee writes caller storage.
fn mid(xs: []const i32) i32 { return xs[1]; } — Zig returns by value for scalar element types; single reading, no aliasing continuation possible for the returned i32.
An explicit tuple/struct return (const Result = struct { q: i32, r: i32 };) — the two results' independence and types are fixed by the struct declaration; single reading.
const r = a * b + c; — same build-mode-dependent overflow ambiguity as F03.P1 (panic in safe modes vs UB in fast modes) attaches to the plain operators; B_i=2.

Zig forces explicit rounding-direction functions for integer division (e.g. @divTrunc) rather than overloading `/` for integers, and requires an explicit conversion for the floating result; each of the three statements has exactly one reading.
std.math.add(i32, m, 1) catch 0; — rung (i), a checked operation yielding an error union with an explicit fallback; single reading.
Explicit `if (b == 0)` guard before @divTrunc — rung (ii); single reading.
std.mem.eql(u8, s1, s2) — the function name itself states a byte-content comparison; single reading, no user-defined/dynamic dispatch possible in Zig for this operation.
std.sort.sort(i32, xs, {}, comparatorDesc) mutates the slice in place by language/library contract; single reading.
std.math.cast(i32, big) — rung (i), returns ?i32; single reading of the out-of-range case (null).
Zig forbids implicit int/float mixing; the required explicit @as/@floatFromInt conversion leaves one reading of which operand's representation changed.
xs[i] — same safe-mode-panic vs fast-mode-UB ambiguity as F03.P1/F07.P1 attaches to plain indexing; B_i=2.
xs[1..4] — Zig slice syntax always denotes a non-copying view over existing storage by language rule; single reading.
var o: ?i32 = null; const n = o orelse 0; — explicit optional type and explicit orelse fallback; single reading.
Zig has no optional-mapping combinator; the substituted explicit if/orelse form has exactly one reading (P-a PARTIAL support, but fully determinate).
try std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10) inside a function whose return type is an error union — `try` is a single, unambiguous propagation marker.
std.fmt.parseInt(...) catch 0; — explicit catch with fallback; single reading of the protected operation and the fallback path.
union(enum) { Circle: f64, Rect: struct{w:f64,h:f64} } — closed by language rule; single reading.
switch on the tagged union without an else arm is compiler-checked for exhaustiveness; single reading of what happens if a case were missing (compile error, not a runtime unhandled case).

Zig has no declared open-extension mechanism for adding a new union case or vtable member from a separate unit without touching the original declaration; the nearest substitute (a manually authored fat-pointer/vtable struct) leaves two materially different readings of how dispatch resolves (direct union-tag switch vs indirect function-pointer call) depending on which substitute pattern a reader assumes without seeing the vtable struct declaration.
fn head(comptime T: type, xs: []const T) T { return xs[0]; } — explicit comptime type parameter with a stated return type T; single reading of the argument/result type relationship.

fn max_of(comptime T: type, a: T, b: T) T using `<` in the body — Zig comptime instantiation deterministically resolves or compile-errors per call; no runtime-observable ambiguity remains at the local form.

An explicit vtable-struct fragment (fat pointer + function pointer field) written out in full in the measured fragment makes the dispatch mechanism and call form fully explicit; single reading given the chosen written form.
ArrayList literal-equivalent construction plus an explicit `for` accumulation loop; single reading, no hidden fold semantics.

std.StringHashMap iteration plus `.get("b") orelse 0` — the optional-returning lookup is a single explicit reading; unspecified iteration order is a single stated language fact, not a branching ambiguity of the local form.
defer file.close(); placed immediately after acquisition — Zig's defer semantics (LIFO, runs once at scope exit on every path including the try-propagated error path) give a single reading.
Zig has no automatic end-of-lifetime hook; the substituted explicit `defer h.deinit()` invoked from a scoped block has one reading (P-a PARTIAL support, fully determinate).
const std = @import("std"); std.debug.print(...) — the import statement's provenance and the introduced name are both explicit; single reading.
pub fn / non-pub fn file-boundary visibility is a compiler-enforced binary; single reading at both the declaration and the external qualified call site.
std.Thread.spawn(...) plus .join() for two units — explicit thread API with an explicit join point; single reading of the concurrency mechanism used.
std.Thread.Mutex explicitly locked around the read-modify-write — single reading of the synchronization discipline used.
extern "c" fn abs(i32) i32; — explicit foreign declaration with explicit C linkage; single reading that the call crosses an FFI boundary.
export fn add2(a: i32, b: i32) i32 { return a + b; } — explicit `export` keyword plus Zig's default C ABI for exported functions; single reading.

metric.semantic_determinacy.probe_basis: 44 fixed probes minus 1 probe with no Zig fragment (F05.P3, excluded per interaction_with_quality_metrics: metrics A-D are computed over probes for which the language has a fragment; a probe scored NONE for this language contributes no fragment and is excluded from this language's own B/log2(B) series, while remaining fully charged in Capability Coverage under its own metric). n_used = 43.
